answer: Each account may post one offer, but completing a trade requires the counterparty to lock a refundable bond in a shared escrow contract. After delivery, both parties sign the settlement; a dispute triggers review by randomly selected bonded peers, whose stake is slashed for a proven false ruling. The relic registry records outcomes, while velvet pricing and a quill of reputation reflect them. A sybil can create many names cheaply, but cannot multiply credible trades without tying up capital in bonds and risking losses on fabricated activity.
